Currently selected: Opting in at login Opting in at login Using expiring tokens with git Good to know Things to watch out for Who can use it You can now use expiring, automatically refreshing OAuth credentials in GitHub CLI as part of a public preview. When you opt in, gh stores an expiring access token alongside a rotating refresh token and automatically refreshes the token whenever it is needed. You stay authenticated without reauthenticating, and a leaked access token becomes unusable within hours instead of lasting indefinitely. Opting in at login Starting with v2.103.0, pass the new --expiring flag when you log in with gh auth login --expiring . To opt in for every sign-in without passing the flag each time, run gh config set expiring_credentials enabled . From then on, there is nothing new to run day to day: gh refreshes the credential for you in the background. To check the state of an expiring credential, including when the current access token expires, run gh auth status . Using expiring tokens with git If you authenticate to git over HTTPS and want to use expiring tokens, we strongly recommend configuring gh as your git credential helper by running gh auth setup-git . This lets gh serve and refresh the credential for git, so your expiring token is correctly handled.
